newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. Western Sahara envoy holds talks in Algiers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Western Sahara envoy holds talks in Algiers.

text.p: The United Nations envoy for Western Sahara, James Baker, held talks with Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual in Algiers on Saturday, the official Algerian news agency APS said.
The former U.S. Secretary of State is on a North African tour to try to relaunch a stalled U.N. peace plan in the disputed territory.
He has said his talks with leaders in Morocco, Algeria, Mauritania and with Polisario Front officials would enable him to prepare a report to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Annan named Baker as his personal representative last month to tackle the dispute over the former Spanish colony, which is claimed by Morocco. The Algerian-backed Polisario Front seeks to establish an independent state there.
"James Baker described his talks with President Zeroual as 'very good' and made clear that his tour in the region is mainly exploratory," said APS.

Baker, who arrived on Friday in Algiers from Morocco where he met King Hassan and other senior officials on the U.N. peace plan and latest developments in the region, also held talks with Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia and Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf.
He was to fly in a Spanish military plane to Mauritania and Tindouf, the Polisario's rear base in southwestern Algeria.

A ceasefire in Western Sahara, monitored by a U.N. force, has held since September 1991 but a plan for a U.N. referendum on the future of the territory has been deadlocked since January 1992 over who is eligible to take part.
